item.title: Man, 61, arrested over fake Chanel, Dior perfumes sold in alleged scam run by his son
item.description: A 61-year-old Hong Kong man has been arrested on suspicion of selling fake luxury perfume in an online scam operation that made more than HK$6 million (US$765,500) in illicit profits over the past two years. Customs officials, who also accused the man of money laundering, said the suspect had operated the Hong Kong side of the business for his 30-year-old son, who is alleged to have masterminded the scam operation from overseas. On Saturday, the Customs and Excise Department revealed that it had... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: "Torturado hasta morir”: la ejecución de un cubano en Texas reabre el debate sobre la pena capital
item.description: Menos de dos meses después de la fallida ejecución de Christa Pike en Tennessee, la pena capital volvió a quedar bajo la lupa el 19 de noviembre, cuando la aplicación de inyección letal a un condenado en Texas tomara más de una hora, mientras el hombre gritaba y se retorcía de dolor, según testigos. Una portavoz del sistema penitenciario del estado sugería que probablemente estaba fingiendo, pero los antecedentes de mal funcionamiento de los fármacos en este tipo de procedimientos arrojan dudas sobre el método. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Hong Kong looks to community networks to support Tai Po fire survivors’ mental health
item.description: More than 3,000 survivors of Hong Kong’s deadly Wang Fuk Court fire have received mental health support from authorities in the past year, with some experiencing fewer symptoms of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) after psychological intervention. Dr Lam Ching-choi, chairman of the Advisory Committee on Mental Health, said on Friday that the government would study whether existing community networks could continue to offer mental health support to people affected by the fire. The committee... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.description: A Chinese PhD student at Princeton University, New Jersey, was detained by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) on Thursday after presenting her research at a neuroscience conference in Washington, the South China Morning Post has confirmed. Eva Yi Xie, a third-year neuroscience student, was detained at Ronald Reagan National Airport in Washington while travelling home from the Society for Neuroscience’s annual meeting, according to a post on social media by her lab, the Brody Lab. It... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: French police officers found guilty of racist assault on black music producer
item.description: Beating of Michel Zecler in 2020 sparked outrage over police brutality after it was caught on security cameras Three French police officers who beat a black music producer they said was not wearing a face mask during the Covid pandemic have been found guilty of intentional, racist violence. The brutal assault on Michel Zecler, now 47, was caught on security cameras in his building in 2020 and triggered outrage in France over police brutality. The trial this month was considered a turning point for the recognition of racist violence. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: ‘Traumatizing’: hunger striker in ICE detention tells of force-feeding ordeal – and what made him crack
item.description: Exclusive: Luis Alejandro Cora Perez says in messages to Guardian from inside Texas facility pain of force-feeding caused him to break strike The text message that came from inside the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention center was stark: “I have spent five days eating regular food. If I don’t eat it, they put the tube in me to feed me.” A Cuban asylum seeker, Luis Alejandro Cora Perez, 32, said in messages to the Guardian this month that he was still weak and dizzy after three months without eating, but that he had broken his hunger strike because being force-fed was just too… Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: China’s rare earth magnet exports to US and EU fall after September rebound
item.description: China’s exports of rare earth permanent magnets to the US and the European Union resumed their decline in October, as Beijing navigated trade relations with both economies. Exports to the US totalled 563.6 tonnes (621.26 short tonnes) last month, down 6.7 per cent from September, according to customs data released on Friday. The decline reversed September’s 18 per cent month-on-month increase and left shipments 14.1 per cent lower than a year earlier. Exports to the EU declined 9.7 per cent... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Pill to treat pancreatic cancer hailed as ‘biggest breakthrough in decades’
item.description: Cancer undetectable for one in 12 patients in daraxonrasib trial, while nearly all participants’ tumours stopped growing A pill that can shrink and potentially eliminate pancreas tumours is being hailed as the biggest breakthrough treatment for the cancer in decades. In one in 12 of the patients given the drug, daraxonrasib , during a trial, the cancer became undetectable, and the tumours stopped growing in almost all of the 61 patients. The trial participants had recently been diagnosed with advanced pancreatic cancer that had spread to other parts of the body. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.
item.dc:creator: Helena Horton

item.description: Exclusive: Guards told their jobs will be transferred to a private contractor that has rejected union recognition The British Library has sparked outrage over plans to outsource its security workforce and hand over to a private company three of its public reading rooms, to be “repurposed” as business spaces for hire – despite having reportedly received millions of pounds from the public purse to refurbish those spaces. Almost 70 guards have been told that their jobs will be transferred to a private contractor, STM, on 1 December. Their union, the PCS, has in turn been informed that STM has… Fuente: The Guardian - World.

In the latest report from the Covid-19 inquiry, the chair, Heather Hallett, also said failures to quickly introduce a test-and-trace system allowed the virus to spread “with deadly speed across the country, virtually unchecked”. item.title: GP dismissed Broome woman's tongue lump before cancer diagnosis
item.description: Monica Frain noticed a lump on her tongue and initially dismissed it after a GP consultation. A dental check-up led to her referral to a specialist who diagnosed her with squamous cell carcinoma. Frain underwent extensive surgery to remove a significant portion of her tongue. Experts emphasize the importance of routine dental examinations for early cancer detection. The case illustrates that timely access to healthcare is vital in regional areas. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: South Korea tightens security for national exam over AI cheating scandal
item.description: More than 550,000 candidates sat South Korea’s Suneung university entrance exam under extraordinary security, after an AI cheating scandal in which a top scorer on a national tax accountant exam admitted using a hidden mini camera to send questions to an AI system. Authorities inspected students’ glasses, deployed thousands of extra supervisors and ordered stickers over every button on candidates’ clothing. A nationwide disaster alert was also sent to make even muted phones buzz, exposing any devices smuggled into exam rooms. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.description: Los fármacos GLP-1 tienen muchas luces , pero también muchas sombras. Llevan años ayudando a pacientes con diabetes a controlar sus niveles de glucosa y desde hace un tiempo también están ayudando a algunas personas a perder peso. Esto último ha llegado a rozar la obsesión en algunas personas, por lo que se advierte a quienes recurren a estos fármacos sin realmente necesitarlos que pueden tener un amplio abanico de efectos secundarios. La mayoría son leves, pero dos reportes de caso publicados recientemente en una revista de psiquiatría nos recuerdan que, en pacientes con problemas previos de… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: Bacteria and viruses team up to hasten the demise of algal blooms
item.description: Nature, Published online: 19 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03606-x Algal blooms are important ecological phenomena that drive carbon fixation and fuel the marine food web. Viral infection often ends them abruptly. Some bacteria can sense infected algal cells and then act in synergy with viruses to expedite a bloom’s collapse. Fuente: Nature.

item.title: Two brain regions tied to memory and emotion may shrink up a decade before Alzheimer’s symptoms
item.description: A groundbreaking study from Johns Hopkins University highlights early brain changes associated with Alzheimer's disease. Specifically, it finds that tissue loss in the entorhinal cortex and amygdala occurs years before hippocampal changes manifest. The research suggests that abnormal tau protein accumulation may play a crucial role in this deterioration. Identifying these early changes could pave the way for timely interventions, enhancing future strategies for Alzheimer's prevention and treatment. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: American couple turned a Volkswagen side hustle into a $30M hammock business
item.description: In 2011, Joe Demin and Rachel Connors embarked on a journey with Yellow Leaf Hammocks, originally as a side venture. Specializing in handwoven hammocks crafted by the Mlabri Tribe in Thailand, the couple faced a turning point during the pandemic. Post-Shark Tank, they pivoted to a direct-to-consumer model, empowering local women through training and crafting. Their dedication culminated in over $30 million in sales, profoundly impacting families. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

Huawei, a Shenzhen-based company, is the world’s largest telecoms equipment maker and a major smartphone manufacturer. item.title: Woman denied medical insurance claim after breast cancer diagnosis
item.description: Jeanette Mozuch bought a cancer policy from Heartland National Life Insurance for extra coverage. After being diagnosed with breast cancer, she filed a claim expecting support for her medical expenses. Heartland denied her claim, stating she answered a question incorrectly on her application regarding mammograms. Mozuch plans to appeal the denial while questioning if other policyholders faced similar issues. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.description: Hongkonger Li Sing-yan has recalled how he “felt like nothing happened” on the day he became one of Asia’s first two kidney cancer patients to receive an incision-free procedure that left him with no wounds or pain, enabling him to eat normal meals by that evening. The cutting-edge technique, called histotripsy, uses focused sound waves to break apart tumours without surgical incisions. The non-invasive medical procedure has already been used to treat more than 400 patients with liver and... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: US loses measles-free status as cases soar
item.description: The United States lost its hard-fought measles elimination status after 26 years, the Pan American Health Organization said on Tuesday, as the country failed to curb the continuous spread of the highly contagious virus for more than a year. Bolivia and Mexico have also lost their measles elimination status, the Americas arm of the World Health Organization said. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.description: El cáncer de páncreas tiene una de las tasas de mortalidad más altas, puesto que no solo es muy agresivo, sino que construye a su alrededor una auténtica coraza biológica. item.description: Exhausted by hefty costs and wedding-planning burnout, some young couples in China are taking an audacious approach to preparing for their big day: turning it into a brand partnership.
